paper.title: A Frequent Construction Mining Scheme Based on Syntax Tree
paper.abstract: Natural language processing (NLP) is one of the main research directions in artificial intelligence. One of the goals of NLP is to identify various semantic information in the text. Currently, the mainstream semantic recognition tasks focus more on using the semantic information of each word in the text to perform semantic analysis of the entire sentence. The research on semantics in cognitive linguistics indicates that semantics is determined by both the words contained in the sentence and the arrangement of the words. Linguists refer to permutations and combinations containing certain semantic information as constructions. Since the construction plays an essential role in semantic information, identifying various constructions in text is a crucial work of semantic recognition tasks. Based on this background, the main works performed in this paper are as follows: 1) The definition and program representation of constructions and the corresponding constraints in NLP tasks are proposed. 2) A frequent construction mining algorithm is proposed to extract frequent structures that meet the construction requirements in the grammar structure tree. Based on the above works, the corresponding construction database can be extracted for the specified natural language corpus, which is helpful for more effective text semantic analysis.

artifact_assessment.evidence: "The corpus can be downloaded from https://corpora.uni-leipzig.de/" (Leipzig Corpora Collection, 2020 English news corpus); no code or mined construction sets are linked.

verdict.summary: A gapped PrefixSpan variant for mining constructions from parse trees, evaluated only by counts, examples and runtime; a numbered prose definition of a standard parse tree and a decorative ξ for minimum support trigger the Level 2 formalism cap.

## Formalism Analysis

### Concept Complexity
**Topic:** Mining frequent "constructions" (form-meaning patterns with gaps, e.g. "What's [NP] doing [PP]") from English text by turning Stanford Parser phrase-structure trees into tree sequences and running a PrefixSpan variant that records how many item sets were skipped between pattern elements.
**Level:** 2 (Low)
**Rationale:** The contribution is a modification of an existing sequential-pattern miner (PrefixSpan with a gap counter and MaxGap/MaxRepeat filters) applied to a new input representation. There is no complexity analysis, correctness argument, or new theory, and the parser is used off the shelf. A simple extension of an existing method applied to a new domain is Level 2.

### Formal Elements
- Definitions: 7 (numbered "Definition 1" to "Definition 7", all in prose; Defs. 6 and 7 introduce the notation Support(α) and the threshold ξ)
- Theorems: 0
- Proofs: 0
- Equations: 0 (the algorithm's pseudocode, Fig. 5, is an image and not part of the text)

### Necessity Test
- Def. 1, construction as a sentence-level form-meaning pair mapped to a structural sequence: Q1 yes, Q2 yes, Q3 no → necessary (fixes that constants may be words or syntactic labels such as NN, NP)
- Def. 2, constant: Q1 yes, Q2 yes, Q3 no → necessary
- Def. 3, empty slot: Q1 yes, Q2 yes, Q3 no → necessary (the gap is what the miner adds to PrefixSpan)
- Def. 4, phrase structure tree: Q1 yes, Q2 no, Q3 no → unnecessary (a textbook description of the parse tree that Stanford Parser already returns; it specifies nothing the implementer builds)
- Def. 5, tree sequence: Q1 yes, Q2 yes, Q3 no → necessary
- Def. 6, support Support(α) as a proportion of the database: Q1 yes, Q2 yes, Q3 no → necessary (fixes the frequency measure, although the paper then works with absolute counts)
- Def. 7, frequent construction, support not lower than ξ: Q1 yes, Q2 yes, Q3 no → necessary as a criterion; the symbol ξ itself is never used again

### Proportionality
Calculated complexity: 14 (7 definitions × 2)
Expected range (Level 2): 0-15
Ratio: 0.93x upper bound

**Assessment:** Proportionate by count. One numbered definition fails the Necessity Test, and the minimum-support parameter is given a Greek symbol that the paper never uses.

### Issues
- Definition 4 restates what a phrase-structure tree is ("each node in the tree represents a syntactic unit in the sentence") as a numbered definition. The tree comes from Stanford Parser and the definition constrains nothing.
- Definition 7 names the minimum support "ξ" and Definition 6 names a sequence "α"; neither symbol appears again, the rest of the paper speaking of "minimum support", MaxGap and MaxRepeat. This is the Greek-letters-for-configuration pattern.
- Definition 6 makes support a proportion, yet the worked example sets "The minimum support is 2" and Table 1 reports raw counts (571151 for "NP IN"). Definition 7 says "not lower than ξ" while Section 4.3 keeps prefixes "whose occurrences exceed the minimum support".
- Seven definitions and no theorem or other formal result.

---

## Citation Analysis

31 references, none with Chen, Peng or Song as author (the C.-M. Chen of [15] and [16] is a PrefixSpan co-author, not this paper's first author). SCR 0/31 = 0%. The references are on topic: construction grammar [1]-[3], graph and sequential pattern mining [4]-[20], parsing [21]-[25] and [28]-[31], structure-aware neural models [26], [27]. Several entries are garbled ("TThe mechanisms", "J.-W. HANY" for J. Han in [5]), a matter of care rather than integrity. No issues identified.

---

## Structural Analysis

The experiments report the number of constructions per minimum support (Fig. 6), the ten most frequent constructions (Table 1), a few hand-picked sentences, and runtime and memory against PrefixSpan (Figs. 7-9). Nothing tests whether the extracted patterns are constructions: there is no gold standard, no precision estimate and no downstream semantic task, so the claims that "the precise mining of frequent constructions is achieved" and that the method can "mine richer semantic information that cannot be identified by traditional methods" are asserted, not shown. The ten most frequent outputs are part-of-speech bigrams such as "DT NN" and "NP IN", and "NP VP" is called "the verb-object construction". The statement that these structures "have been studied in cognitive linguistics, which is consistent with the experimental results" carries no citation. The corpus description is inconsistent: 1,000,000 sentences, then "2.900 million sentences were filtered out", then "290,000 natural sentences". Limitations appear only inline (the runtime cost of gap handling, the extra cost of multi-set sequences, efficiency as future work). CER estimated at about 0.5.

Artifacts: the corpus is the public Leipzig Corpora Collection, cited with its URL. No code, MaxGap/MaxRepeat values or mined construction lists are released.

---

## Conclusion

A modest extension of PrefixSpan to gapped patterns over parse-tree sequences, evaluated only through counts, examples and runtime. The citation record is clean. The formal apparatus is seven prose definitions, of which Definition 4 defines a standard parser output and fails the Necessity Test, and the minimum-support threshold is dressed as ξ without further use. At Level 2 the zero-tolerance rule makes this formalism theater and caps the score. The substantive weakness lies elsewhere: no evidence that the mined patterns are linguistically meaningful constructions.

paper.title: New Opportunities Model for Monitoring, Analyzing and Forecasting the Official Statistics on Coronavirus Disease Pandemic
paper.abstract: At the beginning of 2020, it became obvious that the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic will have a fairly significant scale and duration. There was an unmet need for the analysis and forecast of the development of events. The forecast was needed to make the managerial decisions in terms of knowledge on the dynamics of the pandemic, considering and analyzing the incoming official statistics about the pandemic, modeling and predicting the behavior of this statistics. Due to the objective and subjective factors, the available statistics is far from the unknown true data regarding the pandemic. Therefore, strictly speaking, it was necessary to model and predict not the dynamics of the pandemic, but the dynamics of the official (i.e. government) statistics on the pandemic. This paper proposes a new model, referred to as the new opportunities model, to monitor, analyze and forecast the government statistics on COVID-19 pandemic. A modeling approach is offered in this regard. The modeling approach is important as it answers simple questions on what awaits us in the near future, which is the current phase of the pandemic and when all this will be over. The new opportunities model is applied to three different countries in terms of area, economy and population, namely Russia, Romania and Moldova, plus the Campania region in Italy, and proves to be efficient over other similar models including the classical Susceptible-Infected (SI) model.

flag_details.UNNECESSARY_SET_THEORY: "S = {(ti, Vi, Hi, Di)|i = 0...m}" and "{(ti, Vi, vVi)|i = m − L + 1 . . . m}" use set-builder notation for a list of daily rows and a filtered tail of that list; no proof depends on them.
flag_details.IRRELEVANT_SELF_CITATION: Nine self-citations with topical similarity below 0.3 to COVID-19 statistics forecasting: [9] shape memory alloy actuators, [13] tower crane modelling, [14] fuzzy signatures, [15] observation-process modelling, [17] biomonitoring neural networks, [19] drug-development compounds (book), [25] and [26] slime-mould tuning of fuzzy controllers, [28] particle filter-PSO servo control.
flag_details.ELEVATED_SELF_CITATION: SCR = 10/35 = 28.6%, excluding [36], the paper's own supplementary material (11/36 = 30.6% if it is counted).
flag_details.UNSUPPORTED_CLAIMS: Claims of "high prediction accuracy", outperforming "other similar models" and "superior performance" are made without any accuracy metric, forecast-versus-outcome comparison or competing model in the paper; all results are in an external .doc. CER estimated at about 0.25.

verdict.summary: A piecewise logistic-fitting heuristic for official COVID-19 statistics whose accuracy claims are not shown in the paper; set-builder notation for the data table and nine unrelated self-citations disqualify it.

papers.provenance:
## Formalism Analysis

### Concept Complexity
**Topic:** Forecasting official COVID-19 case statistics by fitting the logistic (called SI) model's phase-plane parabola vV ≈ aV(N − V) to the longest recent window of data that the parabola fits, and switching to a new parabola (a "new opportunity") when the data leave the old one; applied to Russia, Romania, Moldova and Campania.
**Level:** 2 (Low)
**Rationale:** The model is the classical logistic equation and its closed-form tanh solution; the contribution is a piecewise refitting procedure based on parabolic regression. Applying an existing model and regression method to new data, without convergence, identifiability or error analysis, is Level 2.

### Formal Elements
- Definitions: 1 (inline: "current opportunity", the dataset (11) together with its parabola P(V))
- Theorems: 0
- Proofs: 0
- Equations: 15 numbered

### Necessity Test
- Eq. (1), dataset S = {(ti, Vi, Hi, Di) | i = 0...m}: Q1 yes, Q2 no, Q3 no → unnecessary (the daily table of cases, recoveries and deaths written as a set of quadruples)
- Eq. (2), Ei = Hi + Di: Q1 yes, Q2 yes, Q3 no → necessary
- Eq. (3), Si = Vi − Ei: Q1 yes, Q2 yes, Q3 no → necessary
- Eq. (4), seven-day average velocities vΓ with Γ ∈ {V, E, S}: Q1 no, Q2 yes, Q3 no → necessary (fixes window, divisor and zero fill for the first six days)
- Eq. (5), SIR differential system: Q1 no, Q2 no, Q3 no → necessary by the combination rule (Q1 no), although never used afterwards
- Eq. (6), logistic ODE V̇ = aV(N − V): Q1 no, Q2 yes, Q3 yes → necessary
- Eq. (7), k = 0.5aN: Q1 yes, Q2 yes, Q3 no → necessary
- Eq. (8), closed-form tanh solution: Q1 no, Q2 yes, Q3 yes → necessary
- Eq. (9), example parameter values: Q1 yes, Q2 yes, Q3 no → necessary (needed to reproduce Figs. 2-4)
- Eq. (10), τ = tm + 0.5/k ln(N/Vm − 1): Q1 no, Q2 yes, Q3 yes → necessary
- Eq. (11), window {(ti, Vi, vVi) | i = m − L + 1 ... m}: Q1 yes, Q2 no, Q3 no → unnecessary ("the last L days" written in set-builder form)
- Eq. (12), vVi ≈ aVi(N − Vi): Q1 no, Q2 yes, Q3 no → necessary
- Eq. (13), |vVi − aVi(N − Vi)| < ε: Q1 no, Q2 yes, Q3 no → necessary (the window-selection criterion)
- Eq. (14), ti = tm + i − m: Q1 yes, Q2 yes, Q3 no → necessary (forecast indexing)
- Eq. (15), forecast Vi from the tanh solution: Q1 no, Q2 yes, Q3 no → necessary
- Inline definition, current opportunity: Q1 yes, Q2 yes, Q3 no → necessary

### Proportionality
Calculated complexity: 2 (1 definition × 2)
Expected range (Level 2): 0-15
Ratio: 0.13x upper bound

**Assessment:** Proportionate by count, and most equations do real work (the logistic model, its solution, the τ formula, the fitting-window criterion). The two set-builder expressions for the data table and its rolling window fail the Necessity Test.

### Issues
- Eq. (1) "S = {(ti , Vi , Hi , Di )|i = 0...m}" and Eq. (11) "{(ti , Vi , vVi )|i = m − L + 1 . . . m}" are set notation for a list of daily rows and for its last L rows. The letter S is then reused for "people still sick" in Eq. (3).
- Eq. (5) is the SIR system (it has R and γ) although the text calls it the SI model; it plays no part in the method, and Step SI2 fits "the parabola in the right-hand term of (7)" where (6) is meant.
- Broken cross-references: the procedure is announced as "steps NO1 to NO4" but opens with "Step LO1"; Step NO2 says "(9) is next applied to obtain the value of the parameter τ", but (9) holds example values and the τ formula is (10).
- Eq. (4) omits the index i on Γ in the numerator; the threshold is given only as "ε > 1", with no units or chosen value.

---

## Citation Analysis

36 references. Entries with Abramov, Travin, Duca or Precup as author: [9], [13], [14], [15], [17], [19], [25], [26], [28], [35], [36]. [36] is the paper's own supplementary material (a .doc holding Table 1 and Figs. 9-21), not a separate prior work, so I leave it out of both counts: SCR = 10/35 = 28.6%. Counted literally it gives 11/36 = 30.6%, just over the 30% threshold; the outcome does not depend on this choice because of the irrelevant self-citations below.

Topical relevance to forecasting COVID-19 statistics with the logistic model:
- [35] Abramov and Travin, modelling and forecast of COVID-19 statistics in Russia: related (≈0.9)
- [17] neural-network modelling of biomonitoring data, Republic of Moldova: unrelated (≈0.2)
- [9] evolving fuzzy models of shape memory alloy wire actuators: unrelated (≈0.1)
- [13] tensor-product model transformation for tower crane systems: unrelated (≈0.1)
- [14] signatures in fuzzy modelling; [15] observation-process modelling in cognition: unrelated (≈0.1 each)
- [19] book on compounds for drug development (in Romanian), cited for neural networks "for drug development": unrelated (≈0.05)
- [25], [26] slime mould algorithm tuning of fuzzy controllers for servo systems: unrelated (≈0.1 each)
- [28] hybrid particle filter-particle swarm optimization for fuzzy-controlled servo systems: unrelated (≈0.1)

Nine self-citations fall below 0.3. They sit in an introductory catalogue ([1]-[30]) of data-driven modelling and metaheuristic optimization work (financial pricing, bifurcations, data-stream clustering, traffic management, crane modelling, slime-mould, monarch-butterfly and string-theory optimizers), none of which concerns epidemic modelling or is used later. Apart from its own [35], the paper cites no SIR/SEIR or COVID-19 forecasting literature, although it claims to outperform "other similar models". A mutual-citation pattern cannot be established from a single paper, so no ring flag is raised.

---

## Structural Analysis

The central claims (the model "exhibits very good performance, i.e. high prediction accuracy", "outperforms other similar models", and the results "prove the superior performance of the suggested model") have no support in the paper: no error metric, no comparison of past forecasts with realised counts, and no competing model beyond a qualitative look at the plain SI fit for Russia (Figs. 5-7). Table 1 and all result figures (Figs. 9-21) are in an external .doc, and the Results section only narrates them, with slips: Fig. 12 is described twice with different content, its first description saying both that the forecast "did not exhibit oscillations" and that "Rather big oscillations occurred", and "Figure 15 ... for Moldova" appears in the Romanian sequence. The conclusion adds that later pandemic evolution "further confirms the very good performance of the model" without showing it. CER estimated at about 0.25. Limitations: one inline sentence (a parameter must be set by hand) and the acknowledgment that official statistics differ from true incidence.

Artifacts: the data are public, with worldometers country pages linked as [31]-[34] (Campania is linked to the Italian national page). No code is released; the supplement contains results, not software.

---

## Conclusion

A simple, transparent piecewise logistic-fitting heuristic for official COVID-19 counts whose performance claims are not substantiated within the paper. The formalism is mostly functional, but the data table and its rolling window are written in set-builder notation, which at Level 2 triggers formalism theater and unnecessary set theory. The decisive problem is the citation record: nine self-citations on control engineering, fuzzy systems and chemistry unrelated to the topic, with a self-citation ratio of 28.6%. The score is capped.

paper.title: Information: From Cognitive-Sentient Exploration of Reality to Predictive Big Data Assisted Informational Era
paper.abstract: In this article it is shown that information is a concept not only useful and used for the communication systems and data operation, but also for the understanding of the matter non-living and living structuration. On this basis it is described the Informational Model of Consciousness and the functions and operability of the Informational System of the Human Body, allowing to define and understand the Cognitive-Sentient Exploration of Reality used as a tool by our predecessors to create some archaic models of the universe and human, remained up to date as references from philosophic point of view, and still operating nowadays in the creative sciences and arts fields in our informational era. Introducing the concept of information-related matter, it was possible to explain the informational processes in human body and eukaryotic/prokaryotic cells, the basic units of life, and to show that in the living entities an informational system operating similarly with that of the human can be identified and defined as Informational System of the Living Structures. The predictive properties of the Cognitive-Sentient Exploration of Reality is nowadays assisted by the predictive big data analysis, helping in various scientific domains where a high quantity of data was accumulated, including in the bioengineering field and human health, particularly for the prediction of the evolution of COVID-19 cases in the world, with examples for Romania, Spain and USA. Multiple applications involving artificial intelligence and the informational models of human and living structures for a healthy society are mentioned, in particular in neurosciences, biosciences and bioengineering. The priority of the Romanian concepts on information and the important contribution of the Romanian informational science oriented to understand the brain functions/operability and applications in biomedical field is highlighted.
keywords: informational system of the human body

flag_details.EXCESSIVE_SELF_CITATION: 55 of 80 references are by the sole author: SCR = 68.8%.
flag_details.IRRELEVANT_SELF_CITATION: Eight self-citations on silicon technology unrelated to information and consciousness (similarity ≈0.05-0.1): [65], [67], [70] capacitive pressure sensors; [68], [71] boron diffusion and etching; [69] pull-in voltage in polysilicon; [78], [79] atomic transport and impurity diffusion in silicon.
flag_details.THEOREMLESS_FORMALISM: Six relational definitions (more than five) and no theorem or formal result.
flag_details.UNSUPPORTED_CLAIMS: Claims such as solving "the mind-body relation problem", unifying "all theories of psycological and behavior science" and "experimental studies/evidences really support this model" rest only on the author's own earlier papers; the single empirical figure has no error metric. CER estimated at about 0.15.

verdict.summary: A conceptual essay on the author's informational model of consciousness, with pseudo-equations that list system components, a 68.8% self-citation ratio that includes unrelated silicon-sensor papers, and claims resting on the author's own earlier work.

papers.provenance:
## Formalism Analysis

### Concept Complexity
**Topic:** A conceptual essay restating the author's Informational Model of Consciousness and Informational System of the Human Body and of the Living Structures (seven informational centres such as CASI, CDC and IES), connected to ancient philosophy, cell biology and Draganescu's "informatter", followed by a textbook account of ARIMA and an example forecast of COVID-19 cases in Romania, Spain and the USA.
**Level:** 1 (Trivial)
**Rationale:** The paper proposes no algorithm, no validated model and no proof. It is a narrative review of the author's own conceptual framework plus a worked example of an existing forecasting method. Surveys and conceptual reviews are Level 1. It is a research article, not front matter or an editorial, so the EDITORIAL flag does not apply.

### Formal Elements
- Definitions: 6 (relational definitions: ISHB, Eq. 5; the self "I", Eq. 6; ISLS, Eq. 7; inline OIS = CAS+CDC+IES; inline PIS = MIS+GTS+IGG; the inline mapping of informational centres to cognitive centres)
- Theorems: 0
- Proofs: 0
- Equations: 10 numbered, plus inline pseudo-relations and three fitted exponential lines

### Necessity Test
- Eq. (1), I = ΔH = log2 N: Q1 yes, Q2 no, Q3 no → unnecessary (recalled background, never used in any calculation)
- Eq. (2), "Ortomatter" + "Informatter" => Structured Matter: Q1 yes, Q2 no, Q3 no → unnecessary
- Eq. (3), Structured Matter + "Informatter" => Living: Q1 yes, Q2 no, Q3 no → unnecessary
- Eq. (4), (A + B) + I <=> (AB(I)): Q1 yes, Q2 no, Q3 no → unnecessary
- Eq. (5), ISHB = (CASI + CDC + IES + MIS + GTS + IGG + IC): Q1 yes, Q2 no, Q3 no → unnecessary
- Inline OIS = CAS + CDC + IES: Q1 yes, Q2 no, Q3 no → unnecessary
- Inline PIS = MIS + GTS + IGG: Q1 yes, Q2 no, Q3 no → unnecessary
- Inline mapping (CASI, CDC, IES, MIS, GTS, IGG, IC) => (Iknow, Iwant, Ilove, Iam, Icreate, Icreated, Ibelieve): Q1 yes, Q2 no, Q3 no → unnecessary
- Eq. (6), I = (Iknow + Iwant + ... + Ibelieve): Q1 yes, Q2 no, Q3 no → unnecessary
- Inline IA =/= IB: Q1 yes, Q2 no, Q3 no → unnecessary
- Eq. (7), ISLS = (CASI + CDC + IRSS + MIS + GTS + IGG + IC): Q1 yes, Q2 no, Q3 no → unnecessary
- Inline arrow relations (DNA => mRNA => Proteins, IGG=>Icreated, GTS/Ic ==> IGG/Icd): Q1 yes, Q2 no, Q3 no → unnecessary
- Eq. (8), AR(p) expression: Q1 no, Q2 yes, Q3 no → necessary
- Eq. (9), MA(q) expression: Q1 no, Q2 yes, Q3 no → necessary
- Eq. (10), combined ARIMA expression: Q1 no, Q2 yes, Q3 no → necessary
- Fitted lines Cro = 16671×exp(0.01349×t), Csp, Cusa: Q1 yes, Q2 yes, Q3 no → necessary (they are the reported result)

### Proportionality
Calculated complexity: 12 (6 definitions × 2)
Expected range (Level 1): 0-5
Ratio: 2.4x upper bound

**Assessment:** Disproportionate. A conceptual essay carries six relational definitions and a dozen pseudo-equations in which "+", "=" and "=>" stand for "consists of", "corresponds to" and "leads to"; nothing is computed, derived or proved from them.

### Issues
- Eq. (5) "ISHB = (CASI + CDC + IES + MIS + GTS + IGG + IC)" and Eq. (7) use "+" and "=" to list the parts of a system. "OIS=CAS+CDC+IES" and "PIS=MIS+GTS+IGG" do the same inline (with "CAS" for CASI). Eq. (6) writes the self as a sum "Iknow + Iwant + Ilove + Iam + Icreate + Icreated + Ibelieve".
- Eqs. (2)-(3) render Draganescu's view as reaction equations; the sentence after them calls "Ortomatter" the "active agent", whereas the sentence before made informatter the agent and ortomatter the passive substrate.
- The author describes Eq. (4) as "only a schematic convenient representation".
- Eq. (1) is never used: the information contents in Bits quoted for cells are taken from [51].
- Eq. (10) is called ARIMA but has no differencing term (it is an ARMA model); p, d and q are not given; and the "prediction lines" reported for Fig. 3 are single exponentials C = a·exp(bt), not ARIMA output.

---

## Citation Analysis

80 references, 55 of them by the author (F. Gaiseanu): [1], [6]-[18], [21]-[24], [30]-[37], [39], [40], [42]-[50], [52], [56]-[60], [65]-[71], [75], [76], [78]-[80]. SCR = 55/80 = 68.8%.

Topical relevance:
- Unrelated (≈0.05-0.1): [65], [67], [70] silicon capacitive pressure sensors; [68], [71] boron diffusion and etching of silicon; [69] pull-in voltage and stress in polysilicon; [78], [79] atomic transport and impurity diffusion in silicon. They enter through a paragraph on "analytical solutions for nonlinear differential equations to solve the boron diffusion in silicon" inside the section on applications for a healthy society, and through the claim of "a deep experience in science and technology of information [20, 77–79]". Eight self-citations below 0.3.
- Related (≈0.5-0.8): the rest, which present the author's informational model applied to consciousness, attitude, near-death and mystic experiences, plants, epigenetics and COVID-19. They are also the only support offered for the model's claims.

Misattributions: the comparison of "thirteen models ... in 187 countries" is cited to [59] (the author's philosophy paper) when the study is [61]; "a new methodology for verifying the accuracy of time series models" to [56] (the author's paper on plant cells); the ARIMA polynomial to [60] (the author's paper on biotechnology research strategy); ARIMA's "initial work" to [63], a 2020 arXiv preprint. In three of the four cases a self-citation stands where the source of the material should be.

Non-self references include three by F. G. Filip ([20], [72], [77]); [77], on collaborative decision-making, is grouped with the author's silicon papers as evidence of the author's "deep experience", and Filip is thanked in the acknowledgements. A mutual-citation pattern cannot be established from one paper, so no ring flag is raised.

---

## Structural Analysis

The paper makes sweeping claims with no evidence beyond the author's own earlier assertions: recent results allow one "to solve the mind-body relation problem", the model unifies "all theories of psycological and behavior science", "The experimental studies/evidences really support this model" (cited to the author's own [59]), and the power of cognitive-sentient exploration "is proven by the valid results of our ancestors". The conclusions restate them ("It was shown that information is an essential/universal component of reality"). The only empirical content is Fig. 3, 18 days of cases for three countries with exponential fits, without error metric, hold-out period or comparison; the phrase "95% confidence data" is not explained. CER estimated at about 0.15. Limitations: only incidental caveats (relation (4) is "only a schematic convenient representation"; prediction models depend on the data set used); no limitation of the informational model itself is acknowledged.

Artifacts: the COVID-19 example uses data "collected from [61]", a published study; no code, model orders or fitted series are released. The conceptual part has nothing to release.

---

## Conclusion

A conceptual essay that presents the author's informational model of consciousness and of living structures as established, supported almost entirely by the author's own publications (68.8% self-citation, including eight papers on silicon sensor technology unrelated to the topic). Its formal apparatus is notation for lists of named components, which at Level 1 is formalism theater, decorative and disproportionate. The ARIMA section is textbook material with a misstated model and an under-specified example. Disqualified on both formalism and citation grounds.
